understandingEvidence.essentialUnderstandingDe: Für jeden Körper gehört seine eigene Masse zu seiner Geschwindigkeit. In einem gemeinsamen Bezugssystem und zu einem gemeinsamen Zeitpunkt gilt entlang der gewählten Achse p₁ = m₁v₁, p₂ = m₂v₂ und P = p₁ + p₂. Das Vorzeichen gibt die Richtung an.
understandingEvidence.essentialUnderstandingEn: Each object's mass is paired with its own velocity. In a common frame at a common instant, the components along the chosen axis satisfy p₁ = m₁v₁, p₂ = m₂v₂ and P = p₁ + p₂. The sign indicates direction.
understandingEvidence.observablePerformanceDe: Die lernende Person legt für zwei entgegenkommende Wagen eine positive Richtung fest, begründet die Vorzeichen und gibt beide Impulse und ihre Summe in kg·m/s an. Sie erklärt anhand der Produkte, wie der langsamere Wagen die Richtung des Gesamtimpulses bestimmen kann.
understandingEvidence.observablePerformanceEn: For two carts approaching each other, the learner chooses a positive direction, justifies the signs and reports both momenta and their sum in kg·m/s. Using the two products, the learner explains how the slower cart can determine the direction of total momentum.
understandingEvidence.transferExpectationDe: In einer neuen Momentaufnahme bewegt sich nur einer von zwei unterschiedlich schweren Körpern. Die lernende Person bestimmt den Beitrag des ruhenden Körpers und sagt voraus, wie sich der Zahlenwert des Gesamtimpulses bei umgekehrter Achsenrichtung ändert.
understandingEvidence.transferExpectationEn: In a fresh snapshot, only one of two objects of unequal mass is moving. The learner determines the stationary object's contribution and predicts how reversing the axis changes the signed value of total momentum.

descriptionReviews.rationale: Both descriptions specify the two objects, common instant, straight line, sign convention and one requested total. This is a calculation for one state. The conservation law belongs to a later goal.

understandingEvidence.essentialUnderstandingDe: Für denselben Körper fester Masse im Inertialsystem gibt die gerichtete Impulsänderung geteilt durch die verstrichene Zeit die mittlere resultierende äußere Kraft an. Ihre Richtung folgt aus der Änderung des Impulses. Zwei Endwerte lassen den Kraftverlauf dazwischen offen.
understandingEvidence.essentialUnderstandingEn: For the same fixed-mass body in an inertial frame, directed momentum change divided by elapsed time gives the average net external force. Its direction follows from the change in momentum. Two endpoint values leave the intervening force history undetermined.
understandingEvidence.observablePerformanceDe: Aus zwei datierten Impulswerten auf einer Geraden bildet die lernende Person Endwert minus Anfangswert und die positive Zeitspanne. Sie gibt den Quotienten in N an und erklärt, wie bei zwei negativen Impulswerten eine positive mittlere Kraft möglich ist.
understandingEvidence.observablePerformanceEn: From two timed momentum values along a line, the learner finds final minus initial momentum and the positive elapsed time. The learner reports the quotient in N and explains how two negative momentum readings can give a positive average force.
understandingEvidence.transferExpectationDe: In einem neuen Datensatz sind Anfangs- und Endimpuls gleich, während ein Zwischenwert abweicht. Die lernende Person begründet die mittlere Kraft von 0 N über das ganze Intervall und bestimmt aus den Daten die Richtungen der mittleren Kräfte in den beiden Teilintervallen.
understandingEvidence.transferExpectationEn: In fresh data the initial and final momenta are equal, while an intermediate reading differs. The learner justifies a whole-interval average force of 0 N and determines the directions of the average forces in the two subintervals.

descriptionReviews.rationale: The signed inputs, inertial frame, fixed mass, finite interval, force unit and directional interpretation are explicit in both languages. The calculation is accessible at the Klasse 10 placement without calculus.

understandingEvidence.essentialUnderstandingDe: Die Höhe des p(t)-Graphen gibt den gerichteten Impuls an. Für den geradlinig bewegten Körper fester Masse im Inertialsystem gibt die Steigung der Tangente am betrachteten Zeitpunkt die momentane resultierende äußere Kraft an. Ihre Einheit ist (kg·m/s)/s = N.
understandingEvidence.essentialUnderstandingEn: The height of a p(t) graph gives signed momentum. For a fixed-mass body moving along a line in an inertial frame, the tangent slope at the time of interest gives the instantaneous net external force. Its unit is (kg·m/s)/s = N.
understandingEvidence.observablePerformanceDe: An einem unbekannten skalierten Diagramm wählt die lernende Person zwei gut ablesbare Punkte auf der eingezeichneten Tangente, bildet das Steigungsdreieck und schätzt die Kraft mit Vorzeichen und Einheit. Bei negativem Impuls und steigender Tangente begründet sie Bewegungs- und Kraftrichtung getrennt.
understandingEvidence.observablePerformanceEn: On an unfamiliar scaled graph, the learner chooses two readable points on the drawn tangent, constructs a slope triangle and estimates the force with sign and unit. For negative momentum and a rising tangent, the learner explains the directions of motion and force separately.
understandingEvidence.transferExpectationDe: Ein neuer gekrümmter Graph erreicht denselben positiven Impuls zu zwei markierten Zeiten mit entgegengesetzten Tangentensteigungen. Die lernende Person schätzt beide momentanen Kräfte und erklärt, wie sie mit einer mittleren Kraft von 0 N zwischen den Markierungen vereinbar sind.
understandingEvidence.transferExpectationEn: A fresh curved graph reaches the same positive momentum at two marked times with opposite tangent slopes. The learner estimates both instantaneous forces and explains how they are consistent with an average force of 0 N between the marks.

descriptionReviews.rationale: The learner interprets and reads a supplied tangent at a marked time. The book figure correctly uses two points on the tangent to obtain −2 N. Both descriptions preserve the graphical estimate and the one-dimensional model.

understandingEvidence.essentialUnderstandingDe: Im Inertialsystem bestimmt die resultierende äußere Kraft bei konstanter Masse die Beschleunigung. Ihr Betrag ist |F_res|/m. Eine von null verschiedene Beschleunigung zeigt in Richtung der Resultierenden. Die vorhandene Geschwindigkeit kann eine andere Richtung haben.
understandingEvidence.essentialUnderstandingEn: In an inertial frame, the net external force on a constant-mass body determines its acceleration. Its magnitude is |F_net|/m. Nonzero acceleration points along the net force. The existing velocity can point in a different direction.
understandingEvidence.observablePerformanceDe: Die lernende Person formuliert das Gesetz und erklärt für einen nach rechts fahrenden Wagen mit vorgegebener Resultierender nach links, wohin die Beschleunigung zeigt, wie sich die Bewegung zunächst ändert und was eine Verdoppelung der Kraft bei gleicher Masse bewirkt.
understandingEvidence.observablePerformanceEn: The learner states the law and explains, for a rightward-moving cart with a given leftward net force, which way it accelerates, how its motion initially changes and what doubling the force at the same mass does.
understandingEvidence.transferExpectationDe: Zwei bereits bewegte Körper mit den Massen m und 2m erfahren dieselbe quer zur Bewegung gerichtete Resultierende. Die lernende Person vergleicht ihre Beschleunigungspfeile und begründet, was mit der Beschleunigung geschieht, sobald die Resultierende verschwindet.
understandingEvidence.transferExpectationEn: Two moving bodies of masses m and 2m experience the same net force transverse to their motion. The learner compares their acceleration arrows and explains what happens to acceleration when the net force vanishes.

descriptionReviews.rationale: Magnitude and direction express one vector law. The qualification about nonzero acceleration handles the zero vector correctly. The wording works with words and arrows at an earlier stage and leaves force calculations and momentum rates to their respective goals.

descriptionReviews.proposedDescriptionDe: Die lernende Person kann einen einfachen Rückstoß in einem Inertialsystem qualitativ erklären. Dazu betrachtet sie dieselben Körper vor und nach dem Rückstoß als System und nutzt die Gleichheit ihrer vektoriellen Gesamtimpulse, wenn der resultierende äußere Kraftstoß über das betrachtete Intervall null ist.
descriptionReviews.proposedDescriptionEn: The learner can explain a simple recoil qualitatively in an inertial frame. The learner treats the same bodies as the system before and after recoil and uses the equality of their total momentum vectors when the net external impulse over the interval is zero.

understandingEvidence.essentialUnderstandingDe: Bei einem Rückstoß überträgt die innere Wechselwirkung Impuls zwischen den beteiligten Körpern. Ist der äußere Gesamtkraftstoß auf diese Körper null, ist ihre Impulssumme vor und nach dem Vorgang gleich. Bei einem Paar, das anfangs ruht, sind die Endimpulse daher gleich groß und entgegengesetzt.
understandingEvidence.essentialUnderstandingEn: During recoil, the internal interaction transfers momentum between the bodies. If the net external impulse on those bodies is zero, their momentum sum is equal before and after the event. For a pair initially at rest, their final momenta therefore have equal magnitudes and opposite directions.
understandingEvidence.observablePerformanceDe: Für zwei unterschiedlich schwere Wagen, die aus der Ruhe auseinanderrollen, grenzt die lernende Person das System ab und begründet, wann äußere horizontale Einwirkungen vernachlässigbar sind. Sie skizziert die Impulspfeile danach und erklärt, warum der leichtere Wagen schneller ist.
understandingEvidence.observablePerformanceEn: For two unequal-mass carts rolling apart from rest, the learner identifies the system and explains when external horizontal effects are negligible. The learner sketches the final momentum arrows and explains why the lighter cart moves faster.
understandingEvidence.transferExpectationDe: Ein neues Paar driftet vor dem Abstoßen gemeinsam nach rechts. Die lernende Person beurteilt die Vermutung, danach müsse ein Körper nach links fahren. Sie begründet ihre Antwort anhand der entgegengesetzten Impulsänderungen und des positiven Anfangsgesamtimpulses.
understandingEvidence.transferExpectationEn: A fresh pair drifts together to the right before pushing apart. The learner evaluates the claim that one body must then move left, using the opposite momentum changes and the positive initial total momentum.

descriptionReviews.rationale: The original can be read as asserting constancy throughout any interval whose net external impulse is zero. The before-and-after wording gives precisely the conclusion needed for recoil and identifies whose momentum is being compared. It preserves the qualitative demand.

understandingEvidence.essentialUnderstandingDe: Für dieselben Körper in einem gemeinsamen Inertialsystem heben sich nach Newton III die inneren Kraftpaare beim Summieren der Impulsgleichungen aus Newton II auf. Daher gilt dP⃗/dt = ΣF⃗_ext. Das Zeitintegral ergibt ΔP⃗ = J⃗_ext. Ein verschwindender Gesamtkraftstoß liefert Endpunktgleichheit. Für durchgehende Konstanz muss die äußere Resultierende zu jedem Zeitpunkt verschwinden.
understandingEvidence.essentialUnderstandingEn: For the same bodies in a common inertial frame, Newton's third law cancels internal force pairs when the individual momentum equations from Newton's second law are summed. Hence dP⃗/dt = ΣF⃗_ext. Time integration gives ΔP⃗ = J⃗_ext. Zero net impulse gives endpoint equality. Constancy throughout requires the net external force to vanish at every instant.
understandingEvidence.observablePerformanceDe: Die lernende Person wählt System und Intervall, schreibt die Kräfte für jeden Körper mit ihrem Wechselwirkungspartner auf und zeigt, welche Terme erst in der Systemsumme wegfallen. Sie integriert die verbleibende Gleichung, prüft N·s = kg·m/s und formuliert beide Erhaltungsbedingungen.
understandingEvidence.observablePerformanceEn: The learner chooses a system and interval, writes each body's forces with their interaction partners and shows which terms cancel only in the system sum. The learner integrates the remaining equation, checks N·s = kg·m/s and states both conservation conditions.
understandingEvidence.transferExpectationDe: Für ein materiell abgeschlossenes System erhält die lernende Person einen neuen äußeren Kraft-Zeit-Verlauf mit positiver Rechtecksfläche und gleich großer negativer Dreiecksfläche. Sie leitet den Vergleich des Anfangs-, Zwischen- und Endimpulses aus der Bilanz her und erklärt, wie sich der Verlauf von dem bei durchgehend verschwindender äußerer Resultierender unterscheidet.
understandingEvidence.transferExpectationEn: For a fixed set of bodies, the learner is given a fresh external force–time graph with a positive rectangular area and an equal negative triangular area. The learner derives the comparison of initial, intermediate and final momentum from the balance and explains how the momentum history differs from that under zero net external force throughout.

descriptionReviews.rationale: The current descriptions expressly distinguish the interval conclusion from the conditions for continuous conservation. The board image shows the sufficient special case with internal forces only. The full description correctly extends beyond that example.

profileReviews.reason: The cancellation case gives +1.20 and −1.20 kg·m/s with right positive. Both objects move even though P = 0. The stationary-box case gives −3.0 and 0 kg·m/s. Explaining axis reversal and the contribution of a stationary mass tests two different features of the same calculation. The bilingual cases work independently of the pictured equal-mass carts.

Both averages are correct, −2 N and +1 N. The first brief repeats the teaching image's times, momenta and displayed answer. Its midpoint question adds independent reasoning, but the numerical calculation is already disclosed. In the second brief the two negative readings establish leftward motion at the two endpoints.
requiredChanges: Give the reversal brief fresh signed readings or a fresh time table for the independent calculation. Keep the question about what can be inferred at an intermediate time.

In both languages, refer to leftward motion at the two measurement times, or explicitly give continued leftward motion as an additional fact. Two endpoint readings alone leave possible reversals between them open.

profileReviews.reason: The first tangent gives +3 N at negative momentum. In the second case the horizontal tangent gives 0 N and the secant gives +2 N. These are meaningful variations. As written, the first task supplies both tangent coordinates in prose, and the second states that the tangent is horizontal. Both can be answered without demonstrating the specified graph-reading skill.
requiredChanges: For at least one independent brief, use the coordinates as instructions for preparing a fresh scaled diagram. Give the learner the marked instant and drawn tangent, with readable axes, and ask them to select and read their own tangent points.
Keep the signed slope, unit, physical direction and expected numerical range in the reviewer-facing guidance in both languages. Allow a reasonable reading tolerance.

profileReviews.reason: The cases correctly cover a force opposing motion, doubled force, doubled mass and zero resultant. Supplying the resultant keeps the task focused on Newton II. The English expectation says that acceleration direction ‘differs from the direction of existing velocity’. Aligned velocity and acceleration are possible, as the profile's own variation axis recognizes.
requiredChanges: Change the English sentence to ‘The acceleration direction need not coincide with the current velocity direction.’ This matches the distinction made in German. Retain both conceptual cases.

profileReviews.reason: The spring-cart prediction correctly links unequal masses to unequal speeds from initial rest. The astronaut brief requests a final velocity and direction from an unspecified nonzero initial momentum and the package velocity. Those facts do not determine a unique answer. Mandatory numerical inversion, an exact speed ratio and measurement checks also exceed the qualitative recoil goal.
requiredChanges: Use a common inertial frame and a fixed astronaut-plus-package system with negligible external impulse. Give the initial drift direction and how the package's momentum changes. Ask for the direction of the astronaut's momentum change and what can be said about her final direction.

Make the required performance a qualitative, signed before-and-after balance. Keep the lighter-cart prediction. Use supplied numbers or measurements as optional checks, with approximate equality where external effects are negligible.
State in both core expectations when the equality refers to the two endpoints. Reserve a general derivation of continuous conservation for the advanced proof.

profileReviews.reason: The proof expectations correctly require pairwise cancellation, an external impulse balance, units and a distinction between the two conservation conditions. The subsystem and successive-pulse cases expose different parts of the proof. The frame variation can be read as assigning different frames to different bodies in one sum, and the German pulse brief calls the externally pushed system ‘abgeschlossen’ without specifying material closure.
requiredChanges: Specify in both languages that every momentum and force in a given balance is expressed in one common inertial frame. A transfer may repeat the entire analysis in another inertial frame.

Describe the pulse case as a fixed set of carts subject to external forces. In the collision brief, distinguish exact endpoint equality for zero external impulse from approximate equality for a negligible impulse.

Describe the time-history variation in terms of net external force throughout the interval and its integrated impulse over the interval. Retain the two opposite impulses as the endpoint counterexample.

atomicityReviews.reason: The axis and two individual products are necessary steps in constructing one directed total for a single snapshot. Splitting them here would separate the calculation from its sign convention.
independentlyAssessableFacets: Determine and interpret the signed total momentum of two collinear objects at one instant.

atomicityReviews.reason: The time ordering, subtraction, division, unit and direction all characterize the same interval-average force.
independentlyAssessableFacets: Infer the signed average net external force from a body's two timed momenta.

atomicityReviews.reason: Reading the tangent and interpreting its slope as a force are the graphical and physical parts of one estimate at a specified time.
independentlyAssessableFacets: Translate a drawn p(t) tangent into an instantaneous net force with direction and unit.

atomicityReviews.reason: Force scaling, inverse mass dependence, direction and the zero case are consequences of the same constant-mass vector equation.
independentlyAssessableFacets: Explain how a given net force and constant mass determine acceleration in an inertial frame.

atomicityReviews.reason: Choosing the interacting bodies and comparing their endpoint totals supplies one qualitative explanation of recoil. Solving for an unknown velocity is separable and need not be a required facet.
independentlyAssessableFacets: Justify simple recoil with the total momentum balance for the chosen bodies.

atomicityReviews.reason: Cancellation, the differential balance and its time integral form one proof. Distinguishing its instantaneous and interval conclusions establishes when the derived statement holds.
independentlyAssessableFacets: Derive and interpret the system momentum balance from Newton II and III under stated conditions.

prerequisiteReviews.reason: The direct mathematics goals supply signed addition, subtraction, multiplication and division. Their closure provides number and sign conventions. The Physics motivation anchor serves the stated entry contract. Masses, velocities and directions are given, so mastery of a speed-measurement experiment adds no required input. The physical association p = mv is taught here.

IMP supplies signed single-body momentum and axis choice. Its two-body sum is extra preparation for this particular calculation, but removing the edge would also remove the current teaching place for signed momentum. The other direct goal supplies differences over positive intervals, units and the meaning of an average. The body and frame are stipulated. Interpreting this specific rate as net external force remains the new physics.

RATE-M supplies the finite-interval physical comparison. The mathematics goal on derivatives as point slopes brings graph reading, secants, difference quotients and the tangent concept through its closure. The new step is to read a local momentum slope as force. Symbolic differentiation of a fitted function is unnecessary.

Newton I establishes inertial-frame and zero-resultant reasoning. Its closure already includes acceleration, directed motion, qualitative force effects, units and proportional relationships. The magnitude and direction of acceleration for a nonzero resultant remain to be learned. Applying the equation to numerical dynamics problems is a successor.

IMP supplies the signed sum. Applying Newton III prepares the distinction between an interaction pair on two bodies and forces on one body, and its closure already includes the conceptual Newton II goal. The additional gate requiring application of ΣF = ma to accelerated motion contributes no quantity or inference needed for this qualitative endpoint comparison. The external-impulse condition can be introduced through the system boundary here. The formal impulse goal is downstream.

The direct laws-of-motion applications prepare body-by-body force accounting and identification of action–reaction pairs. RATE-I now supplies the single-body dp/dt relation, with signed momentum and RATE-M in its closure. The vector and integral branches supply component sums, signed accumulation and the fundamental theorem. Together they support the proof without assuming its conclusion. Its LK placement requires those mathematics prerequisites to be available when it is taught.

semanticKindReviews.reason: The signed composition of momenta can be taught and demonstrated across different two-body states.

The goal asks for the physical meaning and consequences of a law. Its formula can also support a separate recall task.

Deriving a physical law for a system and identifying its validity conditions is a teachable proof competence. It remains applicable when the system boundary or external force history changes.

limitations: Inspection covered the 45 retained physical pages in all 22 official PDF excerpts, including the printed formula graphics used for the source decisions. All original-publication pages outside those excerpts were uninspected. Page references identify physical PDF pages, which can differ from printed footer numbers.

The 90 supplied views establish current product roles and locations. Source findings concern the six assigned goals and the identified placements. The packet does not establish every historical mapping or a nationwide mandate for the advanced proof.
